Orthonormal bases (singular: basis) are a useful subclass of [[vector space]] bases.

== Formal definition ==

If $(e_1,\ldots,e_n)$

* is an [[orthonormality#Orthonormal_vector_list|orthonormal vector list]] in vector space $V$,
* has length $\dim(V)$, then

$$
\forall v = a_1 e_1 + \cdots + a_n e_n
$$

$(e_1,\ldots,e_n)$ is hence known as an '''orthonormal basis''' for $V$.<ref>{{#cite:Q1930}}</ref>

== Properties ==


Let $(e_1,\ldots,e_n)$ be an orthonormal basis for [[vector space]] $V$.

$$
\forall v\in V
\begin{cases}
v=\sum_{k=1}^n \langle v,e_k\rangle e_k \\
\lVert v\rVert^2=\sum_{k=1}^n |\langle v,e_k\rangle|^2
\end{cases}
$$

{{Hidden proof}}
$$
\because v = a_1 e_1 + \cdots + a_n e_n & \text{(1)} \\
\therefore \forall k \in \{1, \cdots, n\}, \langle v, e_k \rangle= \langle a_1 e_1 + \cdots + a_n e_n , e_k \rangle = a_k \\
\therefore \text{(1) becomes } v =  \langle v, e_1 \rangle e_1 + \cdots + \langle v, e_n \rangle e_n \\
\text{i.e., } v=\sum_{k=1}^n \langle v,e_k\rangle e_k \\
$$

and

$$
\lVert v\rVert^2=\sum_{k=1}^n |a_k|^2=\sum_{k=1}^n |\langle v,e_k\rangle|^2
$$
{{End hidden}}
